chapter.li: LEChapter24 Verse1 Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came unto the sepulcher, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them. VerseEnd Verse2 And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulcher, and two angels standing by it in shining garments. VerseEnd Verse3 And they entered into the sepulcher and, not finding the body of the Lord Jesus, VerseEnd Verse4 they were much perplexed thereabout, VerseEnd Verse5 and were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth. But behold, the angels said unto them, Why do you seek the living among the dead? VerseEnd Verse6 He is not here, but is risen. Remember how he spoke unto you when he was yet in Galilee, VerseEnd Verse7 saying, The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again? VerseEnd Verse8 And they remembered his words, VerseEnd Verse9 and returned from the sepulcher, and told all these things unto the eleven and to all the rest. VerseEnd Verse10 It was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women who were with them, who told these things unto the apostles. VerseEnd Verse11 And their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not. VerseEnd Verse12 Then arose Peter, and ran unto the sepulcher, and went in. And he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves. And he departed, wondering in himself at that which had come to pass. VerseEnd

Verse13 And behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem sixty furlongs. VerseEnd Verse14 And they talked together of all these things which had happened. VerseEnd Verse15 And it came to pass that while they spoke together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near and went with them. VerseEnd Verse16 But their eyes were held, or covered, that they could not know him. VerseEnd Verse17 And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these which you have one with another as you walk and are sad? VerseEnd Verse18 And one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Are you a stranger in Jerusalem and have not known the things which have come to pass there in these days? VerseEnd Verse19 And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet, mighty in deed and word before God and all the people, VerseEnd Verse20 and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death and have crucified him. VerseEnd Verse21 But we trusted that it had been he who should have redeemed Israel. And besides all this, today is the third day since these things were done, VerseEnd Verse22 yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished who were early at the sepulcher. VerseEnd Verse23 And when they found not his body, they came, saying that they had also seen a vision of angels who said that he was alive. VerseEnd Verse24 And certain of them who were with us went to the sepulcher and found even so as the women had said, but him they saw not. VerseEnd

Verse25 Then he said unto them, O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken. VerseEnd Verse26 Ought not Christ to have suffered these things and to enter into his glory? VerseEnd Verse27 And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself. VerseEnd

Verse28 And they drew near unto the village to which they went, and he made as though he would have gone further, VerseEnd Verse29 but they constrained him, saying, Abide with us, for it is toward evening and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them. VerseEnd Verse30 And it came to pass, as he sat at a meal with them, he took bread and blessed, and broke, and gave to them. VerseEnd Verse31 And their eyes were opened, and they knew him, and he was taken up out of their sight. VerseEnd Verse32 And they said one to another, Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked with us by the way and while he opened to us the scriptures? VerseEnd

Verse33 And they rose up the same hour and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them, VerseEnd Verse34 saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon. VerseEnd Verse35 And they told what things they saw and heard in the way, and how he was known to them in breaking of bread. VerseEnd

Verse36 And as they thus spoke, Jesus himself stood in the midst of them and said unto them, Peace be unto you. VerseEnd Verse37 But they were terrified and afraid, and supposed that they had seen a spirit. VerseEnd Verse38 And he said unto them, Why are you troubled? And why do thoughts arise in your hearts? VerseEnd Verse39 Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I, myself; handle me and see, for a spirit has not flesh and bones as you see me have. VerseEnd Verse40 And when he had thus spoken, he showed them his hands and feet. VerseEnd

Verse41 And while they yet wondered and believed not for joy, he said unto them, Have you here any food? VerseEnd Verse42 And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish and a honeycomb. VerseEnd Verse43 And he took it and did eat before them. VerseEnd Verse44 And he said unto them, These are the words which I spoke unto you while I was yet with you — that all things must be fulfilled which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. VerseEnd Verse45 Then opened he their understanding that they might understand the scriptures, VerseEnd Verse46 and said unto them, Thus it is written: And thus it behooved Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day, VerseEnd Verse47 and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse48 And you are witnesses of these things. VerseEnd Verse49 And behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you; but remain in the city of Jerusalem until you are endowed with power from on high. VerseEnd

Verse50 And he led them out as far as to Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them. VerseEnd Verse51 And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he was taken from them and carried up into Heaven. VerseEnd Verse52 And they worshipped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy, VerseEnd Verse53 and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen. VerseEnd
